findingDetails.title: The README says a stored run line holds no offeredAs, but both current writers store it
findingDetails.claim: The blanket sentence 'A stored run line holds no offeredAs, so its offer counts as before' is false for a line written by either current writer, because both writers keep the field and the scorer uses it to split partner from head.
findingDetails.evidence: command-offer.mjs:496 writes offeredAs on a backfilled line; run-command-behaviour.mjs:1203 spreads offerLineFields, which writes it at :824; score-command-transcripts.mjs:1471-1476 reads line.offeredAs.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether 'stored' is defined as the pre-field corpus only. The README's own --brief-only paragraph at :85 says a field may be present or absent, so the document already knows a stored line can hold it.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The sentence was written when only legacy lines existed and was not updated after T006/T007.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Withdraw if a later definition names 'stored' as the pre-offeredAs corpus only.
findingDetails.case: A live line written at run-command-behaviour.mjs:1201-1205 carries offeredAs 'partner'; offerOf counts it in offeredAsPartner and not in offered, while README.md:123 says a stored line holds no offeredAs and counts as before.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The README is the changed accuracy-runner path in review-scope-4c.txt; both writers and the scorer are the brief's verification surfaces.

findingDetails.title: The runner row says --brief-only rewrites the four fields, but that mode copies the offer fields untouched
findingDetails.claim: The runner row's [--brief-only] clause promises a four-field rewrite, but the brief-only branch copies the input line and changes only briefDelivered and briefBackfilled, so a legacy line keeps no offer fields.
findingDetails.evidence: command-offer.mjs:489-490 builds { ...line, briefDelivered, briefBackfilled } when briefOnly; the else branch at :492-500 writes the four offer fields. README.md:85 says brief-only keeps every offer field as the input holds it.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether --brief-only is rejected with --backfill or scoped differently in the run options; run-command-behaviour.mjs:1067-1082 accepts the pair, and the row names both in one sentence.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: 'Rewrites with' could mean the output may hold the fields when the input does; the paragraph at :85 is the precise statement, and the row is the imprecise one.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Withdraw if the row is read as describing the default backfill only and the bracket is treated as a separate mode heading.
findingDetails.case: A legacy line with no offeredCommand, offeredPolicy or offeredAs, run through --backfill --brief-only; the output has briefDelivered and briefBackfilled but none of the three offer fields, contradicting the runner row.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The README is the changed accuracy-runner path; the backfill branch is the writer the row describes.
